title: Adaptive soft-priority triage and hedged model-paths for GPU memory resilience
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: We continue to see tail OOM events on high-concurrency endpoints when uncommon long-sequence requests collide with heavy KV cache residency and wide batching windows. Current mitigations (hard eviction thresholds and coarse fallback models) are either too aggressive (causing quality regressions) or too slow to prevent spikes in request latency/failed responses.

Goal: Introduce an adaptive soft-priority triage layer that: (1) tags and ranks inflight requests by a combination of request cost estimate and service-level priority, (2) opportunistically shrinks batch admission and KV residency for low-priority work, and (3) hedges between a fast narrow-path model and a lower-memory slow-path model with transparent retry and quality-preservation heuristics. The approach should prevent hard OOMs, preserve high-priority quality, and minimize visible regressions to customers.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end tests reproduce previous OOM pattern and show no hard OOMs after deploying the triage layer in canary with traffic shaping
P99 latency for high-priority requests remains within 1.25x of baseline in the canary cluster
Quality regressions measured on our eval prompt set for high-priority routes are <2% relative drop vs baseline; low-priority allowed up to 8%
Operational telemetry surfaces a new 'triage_action' tag and shows correct distribution of actions (admit, shrink, hedge, spill) per hour
Rollback plan validated: can toggle triage layer off without requiring node restarts and fall back to existing eviction policy
implementation_plan: Design sprint (2 days): finalize priority scoring function combining estimated token cost, kv-hit-rate, user tier, and SLA label
Runtime change: admission controller middleware to compute per-request soft-priority and decide admit/shrink/hedge/spill
KV cache shim: introduce transient 'soft-slim' residency class where prefix KV entries are stored in compacted/evicted-on-idle mode
Hedged model-paths: implement an orchestrator that races a narrow-quantized variant (low-memory, fast) against the full model if resources permit
Retry semantics: two-phase retry — immediate hedged response if narrow path finishes first; background reconciliation with full-path result when available; reconcile if quality delta > threshold
Prefetch signal: when admitting a request at reduced residency, emit prefetch hints to warm hot-kv for subsequent requests in the same cohort
Configuration knobs: per-route soft_priority_weights, shrink_factor, hedge_timeout_ms, allowed_quality_delta
Safety net: if global GPU memory pressure exceeds emergency watermark, transition triage to full-shed (deny low-priority admit) and surface incident metric
tradeoffs_and_notes: Pros: avoids hard OOMs, preserves high-priority request quality, reduces need for manual operator intervention
Cons: increased system complexity; requires careful tuning of priority weights and hedging timeouts to avoid double work and cost blowups
Quality risk: narrow-path models may systematically underperform on certain prompt families — we will maintain per-route evals and can disable hedging by route
Cost risk: hedging can increase GPU cycles if both narrow and full paths are used; mitigated via hedging timeouts and cohort sampling
Operational note: telemetry must include per-request memory delta, kv-residency-state, and hedged-path latency to diagnose regressions
monitoring_and_rollout: Phase 1 (lab): unit + integration tests, run against synthetic workload that reproduces long sequence collisions
Phase 2 (canary): enable triage for 5% traffic on a dedicated canary pool with aggressive telemetry
Phase 3 (staged roll): increase to 25% then 60% with automated check gates on OOMs, error rates, and quality regression metrics
Phase 4 (global): enable by default with adaptive defaults and route-level overrides
SLOs and alerts: create real-time alert when triage_action='spill' rate > 1% AND cluster memory pressure > 85%
Dashboard: new Runtime > Memory Safety dashboard with triage_action breakdown, hedged-vs-full success ratio, and cost delta estimate
testing_plan: Unit tests for priority scoring and admission decisions
Integration tests with mocked KV shim to validate soft-slim residency semantics
Load tests: replay production traces that caused OOMs and measure failure modes across variable batch sizes
Golden evaluation: run eval suite against hedged narrow-path variants and compute per-route quality deltas
Chaos tests: inject artificial GPU memory pressure and verify graceful degradation path triggers and no hard OOMs
